businessModel: Open-source project funded by Igalia, grants (NLnet) and partnerships; no ads
updateCadence: Regular releases; the GitHub repo was last updated on 2026-10-13
summary: Wolvic is an independent, open-source browser for standalone XR headsets, continued by Igalia from Firefox Reality. It runs on Quest, Pico, Magic Leap 2, Lynx and Huawei glasses, and ships Gecko and Chromium builds.
bestFor: Headset owners who want a non-Meta browser
Open-source and Gecko fans on XR devices
Pico, Lynx or Huawei headset users
notFor: People who want a polished, feature-rich desktop-class browser
Anyone who needs strong ad blocking out of the box

pros.title: Open and independent
pros.detail: MPL-2.0 project maintained by Igalia, not tied to a headset maker.

pros.title: Wide device support
pros.detail: Quest, Pico 4 and Neo 3, Magic Leap 2, Lynx R1 and Huawei glasses.

pros.title: Two engines
pros.detail: A Gecko build and a Chromium build, chosen per need and device.

pros.title: VR video focus
pros.detail: The latest Gecko release adds VR video projection modes.

cons.title: Small team
cons.detail: A smaller project than Meta’s or Pico’s own browsers.

cons.title: Some video sites block it
cons.detail: A Chromium update restored support for VR video sites that had begun blocking non-Meta browsers.

cons.title: Sparse docs on privacy
cons.detail: Ad blocking and tracking-protection details are not clearly documented.

faq.q: Is Wolvic the successor to Firefox Reality?
faq.a: Yes. Mozilla handed the project to Igalia in 2022, which continued it as Wolvic.
Quest 2, Pro, 3 and 3S, Pico Neo3 and Pico 4, Magic Leap 2, Lynx R1 and Huawei Vision Glass and VR Glass.
Its site lists extension support; which store or API it uses is not documented there.

timeline.event: Igalia takes over Firefox Reality as Wolvic
NLnet-funded UI work begins, including a Chromium-based build
Latest Gecko release moves to Gecko 153 ESR; Chromium build 1.2.3 out

switching.note: Sync with desktop is advertised; no importers are documented.

jsSpeed: SpiderMonkey or V8 on headset-class hardware
memory: Shares headset RAM with the system
accessibility: Accessibility fixes in the latest release
beginnerFriendly: Simple headset UI; setup via APK on some devices
